definition: The Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL) is a youth behavioral screening measure made up of items about attention and behavior problems. In the supplied source, a 34-item CBCL was used as the basis for creating a shorter version to help screen for ADHD while also reflecting broader behavior difficulties that can occur alongside it.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly describe the original CBCL as being “made up of items about attention,” nor does it characterize the CBCL itself (prior to reduction) as a screening measure with items specifically about attention; it only states the study reduced the CBCL to create an ADHD screening tool (CBCL-10) targeting youth attention/behavior problems.

The claim that the shorter version “reflect[ed] broader behavior difficulties” is only partially supported: the paper discusses that ADHD screening tools should capture co-occurring problem behaviors (e.g., oppositional/conduct-related behaviors) in general, but it does not directly connect those “broader behavior difficulties” to the content of the specific 10-item instrument in the provided excerpt.
